root_cause: Channel rules and learning existed, but provider side effects were not cryptographically bound to one central authorization decision. A component could hold transport credentials and act after or outside semantic policy validation; provider-scheduled state could also outlive an internal BLOCKED state.
prevention_rule: Every external social side effect requires a short-lived one-time capability issued from canonical database state and bound to run date, channel identity, exact text hash, exact final-media hash and policy version. Instagram additionally requires exact-final Mira vision proof and OpenArt lineage. Invalid scheduled provider state must be cancelled and read back as contained; internal BLOCKED alone is not containment. CI forbids direct provider side-effect primitives outside the canonical publisher.

evidence.incident: A generic Bedrijfsgeheugen Instagram post was visible after Mira-only behavior had already been documented and learned.
evidence.terminal_rule: Not LIVE until merged, deployed and production readback proves authority plus containment.
evidence.provider_containment: Invalid scheduled Instagram provider state must reach CONTAINED only after external cancellation succeeds.
